t:
The Secretary shall, in fulfilling his responsibilities under this Act, select program activities and set priorities which are consistent with the following criteria:

    (1) 
realization of energy production costs for ocean thermal energy conversion systems that are competitive with costs from conventional energy production systems;
 
    (2) 
encouragement of projects for which contributions to project costs are forthcoming from private, industrial, utility, or governmental entities for the purpose of sharing with the Federal Government the costs of purchasing and installing ocean thermal energy conversion systems;
 
    (3) 
promotion of ocean thermal energy conversion facilities for coastal areas, islands, and isolated military institutions which are vulnerable to interruption in the fossil fuel supply;
 
    (4) 
preference for and priority to persons and domestic firms whose base of operations is in the United States as will assure that the program under this Act promotes the development of a United States domestic technology for ocean thermal energy conversion; and
 
    (5) 
preference for proposals for pilot and demonstration projects in which the respondents certify their intent to become an integral part of the industrial infrastructure necessary to meet the goals of this Act.

fable.w: The section only lists substantive criteria the Secretary must apply when selecting program activities and setting priorities. The tempting reading is that references to cost contributions from private, industrial, utility, or governmental entities and to respondents' proposals bring outsiders into the decision. But these are cost-sharing and proposal (application-like) features, not consultation, comment, hearing, advisory committee, or a right to sue. No outside party is consulted before the federal decision.
fable.s: select program activities and set priorities which are consistent with the following criteria

opus.w: The section lists criteria the Secretary uses on his own to choose program activities and set priorities. Outside entities show up only as cost-sharers or as respondents submitting project proposals, which is like applying for grants or contracts and does not count as participation. Nothing here requires the Secretary to consult outsiders, take public comment or hold a hearing before deciding.
opus.s: preference for proposals for pilot and demonstration projects in which the respondents certify their intent to become an integral part of the industrial infrastructure necessary to meet the goals of this Act.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions private, industrial, utility and governmental entities sharing costs, and respondents submitting proposals. That reading fails the definition. These outside parties only fund projects or compete for project awards, which counts as applying for something. The section creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation or right to object before the Secretary sets priorities.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines criteria for the Secretary's internal decision-making process regarding program activities and priorities. It does not require consultation, coordination, or participation from outside parties (such as public hearings, advisory committees with non-federal members, or comment periods). The mention of 'private, industrial, utility, or governmental entities' refers to sources of funding or proposal submitters, not participants in the federal decision-making process. Applying for projects or having proposals evaluated against criteria is not considered participation under the definition.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall, in fulfilling his responsibilities under this Act, select program activities and set priorities which are consistent with the following criteria:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "preference for... persons and domestic firms" or "encouragement of projects... from private... entities" implies a process where these outside parties participate in the decision-making. However, the text only lists criteria for the Secretary's internal selection process. It does not mandate that the Secretary consult with, hold hearings for, or form an advisory board with these outside parties. The interaction described is the submission of proposals (which is akin to an application or grant process, explicitly excluded) and the Secretary's unilateral evaluation based on set criteria. There is no requirement for the outside parties to be involved in the *decision* itself, only that their proposals meet certain criteria.
